messages:
alex: Heads-up: we're seeing short, high-amplitude egress spikes from tenant-124 in us-west-2 that coincide with GPU tail latency jumps (~150ms -> 800ms) on shared pools. Suspect noisy KV-cache regen + network bursts. Looking for quick mitigations and a longer-term preemptive egress guard.
maria: Ugh. saw telemetry too. spikes at 15:12, 15:28, 15:42 — roughly every 16m. any repro steps or logs?
alex: here's a small tail of the proxy logs showing the burst pattern:
```
2026-03-21T15:12:03Z tenant=124 egress_bytes=124MB tokens=230 latency_p90=820ms
2026-03-21T15:12:04Z tenant=124 egress_bytes=98MB  tokens=180 latency_p90=760ms
2026-03-21T15:28:02Z tenant=124 egress_bytes=140MB tokens=240 latency_p90=880ms
```
sam: @alex can you check whether tenant-124 is on shared-gpu-slice or dedicated pool? that changes options.
alex: shared-gpu-slice. They were moved during last week's compaction. switching back to Dedicated would cost ~2.4x for reserved hours.
jess: Quick mitigations:
- throttle egress at the proxy for tenant-124 (soft cap)
- enable short-lived prefetch KV caches throttling
- route their late-stage requests through blue-path (lower throughput, lower egress) while we triage
maria: I can push a soft egress cap. proposal: cap to 50MB/s for 60s windows, and if repeated >3 times in 10m then apply a 5m cooldown + warm-pool prefill for neighbors.
ops-lee: That cooldown rule makes sense. be careful with retries — apps might retry and amplify. add circuit-breaker on request rate, not just bytes.
alex: running a quick probe now. command I'm using:
```
# apply soft proxy cap
curl -X POST https://infra-api/preemptive-guard -d '{"tenant":"124","egress_cap_mb_s":50,"window_s":60}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $API'
```
infra-bot: deploy started: preemptive-guard v2 -> proxy-usw2 (canary 5%). Watching metrics.
sam: cost question: if we move tenant-124 to a small dedicated slice during peak windows, what is the monthly delta? I estimated ~+$1.8k/mo for burst-hours reservation. not ideal but keeps SLAs.
jess: as a compromise: automated warm-pool carveouts for 10m blocks when a tenant hits 3 spikes in 30m. cheaper than full dedicated and protects neighbors.
maria: agreeing. also can we add a telemetry rule to flag correlated KV-regen + egress bursts so we can block preemptively? :thinking:
alex: yes — I'll add a rule to the anomaly detector: if KV-regen_rate > 1000/s AND egress_mb_in_1m > 80 => alert + soft-cap. keeping probe running now, will report after 10m.
ops-lee: also please add a runbook snippet for Support so they can explain transient slowdown to customers (one-pager).
alex: done. I'll update the runbook and post link here once it's live. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
